split: Adaptively selected development comparisons; no held-out or generalization-rate claim.
selection: The selected v22 development matrices, the corrected-geometry pitch comparison, and the earlier cube-only LP comparison are preserved below. This is not an exhaustive history of every attempted variant.
limitations: Matrices differ, seeds and scenes repeat, and candidate changes were guided by these outcomes. Group and case denominators describe their own matrices only. Do not combine successes into a generalization success rate.
runtime_boundary: CPU policy. RGB-D, wrist RGB, camera calibration, robot proprioception/IK, and public task goals only; no simulator object truth or evaluator feedback is returned to the policy.
sensor_scope: Each group sensor is verified against every included result. Historical manifests lacking sensor metadata are supplemented by their recorded per-trial sensor fields.
success_definition: Recorded evaluator success, including physical tower stability; policy completion notes alone are not success.
artifact_scope: Portable public goals, candidate hashes, sensor settings, evaluation outcomes, policy errors and final policy notes only. No images, rollout states, object truth, or absolute paths.

cpu_scope: Each trial retains its recorded CPU profile and exact scope. Worker policy compute excludes simulator/rendering, RPC serialization, and host robot IK; robot IK CPU time is recorded separately. These trial profiles are not isolated algorithm microbenchmarks.

pitch_comparison.decision: Rejected. Retain corrected geometry with the ordinary controller; none of the five activated pitched trials reached opening.
pitch_comparison.scope: Adaptive development. Pitch baseline records are already included in the v22_random/random_l3 group and are not duplicated.

lp_comparison.scope: Bounded adaptive development experiment; six new physical trials paired with six existing frozen-v21 results. No held-out or generalization-rate claim.
lp_comparison.runtime_inputs: Only visual cube models, learned volume mass ratios, existing six-second visual velocity predictions, public goals and robot proprioception.
lp_comparison.change: Replace only cube-prefix weighted target choice with a three-variable LP maximizing the minimum predicted upper-substack COM support-edge margin. Preserve release-drift compensation and controls. Enforce a conservative16-sided inscribed approximation to the existing6mm radial target bound and break LP ties nearest the weighted target.
lp_comparison.unchanged: Frozen v21 perception, grasp, release sequence, sensor, scene generation, physics and strict evaluator.
lp_comparison.cpu_solver: scipy.optimize.linprog using HiGHS, threads=1; no GPU policy component.
lp_comparison.analytic_check: For two equal cube supports centered at0 and-2mm in X, the LP recovered the closed-form new X=-2/3mm and minimum margin13+2/3mm within30nm.
lp_comparison.recommendation: Retain existing weighted balancing. Physical success regressed from4/6 to3/6; objective gains do not establish stable tower dynamics.
interpretation: Seed908 with no distractors regressed from stable to full collapse.
Seed907 with two distractors improved partial score0 to1 and removed support-margin violations, but still failed the strict3mm drift criterion.
Seed909 with two distractors still failed angular-motion stability.
All six LP trials visually completed four levels, but only three passed physical evaluation.
lp_comparison.numerical_note: Logged pre-LP margins refer to the raw weighted reference before release compensation and final target clipping, not to a separately replayed baseline action. The paired physical outcomes, rather than these objective values, determine the recommendation.
lp_comparison.offline_boundary: Private evaluator outcomes/stability reasons are retained only for experiment assessment and were never returned to candidate runtime.
